sahneler.metin: A dam above Williamsburg, Massachusetts, burst one morning.
Floodwater swept through four villages, and one hundred thirty nine people died.
The dam had been built about a decade earlier.
Its design had been changed to save money.
Seepage weakened the embankment until it slid away.
A dam keeper rode to warn people downstream.
Massachusetts then passed laws requiring dam inspections.
